"Which of the following shows the region in the $uv$-plane where the transformation $T,$ given by

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v\end{bmatrix}⟶\begin{bmatrix}u + 3 \\ \left(v + 1\right)^{2}\end{bmatrix},
$$

is (locally) orientation-preserving?" :question/worked-solution "Recall that a transformation is (locally) orientation-preserving at the points where the Jacobian determinant is positive:

$$
\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}>0
$$

We have

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v\end{bmatrix}⟶\begin{bmatrix}u + 3 \\ \left(v + 1\right)^{2}\end{bmatrix}.
$$

Computing the corresponding Jacobian determinant, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)} &=\begin{vmatrix}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 v + 2\end{vmatrix} \\ &=(1)\cdot (2 v + 2)-(0)\cdot (0) \\ &=2 v + 2.\end{aligned}
$$

To find the required regions, we solve the following inequality:

$$
\begin{aligned}2 v + 2 &>0 \\ v > -1\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that the equation

$$
v = -1
$$

defines a horizontal line.

Therefore, the region where the transformation is (locally) orientation-preserving must be the following:

"Which of the following shows the region in the $uv$-plane where the transformation $T,$ given by

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v\end{bmatrix}⟶\begin{bmatrix}v + \left(u + 3\right)^{2} + 1 \\ - 3 u - \left(v + 1\right)^{2} - 9\end{bmatrix},
$$

is (locally) orientation-preserving?" :question/worked-solution "Recall that a transformation is (locally) orientation-preserving at the points where the Jacobian determinant is positive:

$$
\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}>0
$$

We have

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v\end{bmatrix}⟶\begin{bmatrix}v + \left(u + 3\right)^{2} + 1 \\ - 3 u - \left(v + 1\right)^{2} - 9\end{bmatrix}.
$$

Computing the corresponding Jacobian determinant, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)} &=\begin{vmatrix}2 u + 6 & 1 \\ -3 & - 2 v - 2\end{vmatrix} \\ &=(2 u + 6)\cdot (- 2 v - 2)-(1)\cdot (-3) \\ &=- 4 u v - 4 u - 12 v - 9.\end{aligned}
$$

To find the required regions, we solve the following inequality:

$$
\begin{aligned}- 4 u v - 4 u - 12 v - 9 &>0 \\ \left(u + 3\right) \left(v + 1\right) < \frac{3}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

This gives the solution $v < -1 + \frac{3}{4 \left(u + 3\right)}$ for $u>-3$ and $v > -1 + \frac{3}{4 \left(u + 3\right)}$ for $u<-3.$ At $u=-3,$ the Jacobian is positive, so this line belongs to the required region.

Notice that the equation

$$
v = -1 + \frac{3}{4 \left(u + 3\right)}
$$

defines a hyperbola.

Therefore, the region where the transformation is (locally) orientation-preserving must be the following:
